prompt:
Links with a fragment are only half checked today: '#usage' is accepted as it is, and 'guide.md#install' only checks that guide.md exists. Add a command that checks fragments against the headings of markdown documents. It runs as `python -m linkcheck.anchors ROOT REPORT_JSON`.

Look at every markdown document (.md or .markdown) under ROOT, and skip the same folders that the normal scan skips. A heading is a line that starts with one to six '#' characters followed by a space, outside fenced code blocks. Each heading defines one anchor: take the heading text, remove the spaces around it, make it lowercase, remove every character that is not a letter, a digit, a space or a hyphen, and turn each space into a hyphen. When an anchor occurs again in the same document, the second one gets '-1' appended, the third '-2', and so on.

Check every link in these documents that has a fragment. A link that starts with '#' points into its own document. A local link to a .md or .markdown file points into that file; resolve the file part the same way the normal scan resolves local links, with ROOT as the site root. External links, links without a fragment and fragments into other file types are not part of this check. The fragment must equal one of the anchors of the target document.

Checking one link must report a failed check to its caller, with the message `missing file: <link as written>` when the target document does not exist or cannot be read, and `missing anchor: #<fragment>` when no anchor matches.

Write REPORT_JSON as an object with two keys: "documents", the number of markdown documents checked, and "problems", a list with one object per failed link, with the keys "document" (the location of the document that contains the link, under ROOT, with forward slashes), "line", "link" (as written) and "message". Sort the problems by document, then by line. The command exits with status 0, also when problems are found. If ROOT is not a folder, the command exits with status 2 and does not create REPORT_JSON.

Add tests for the new feature. Give every new public function a docstring that describes its parameters and return value.
